haiku-low.q1: Breach streak reaches 3 consecutive breaching evaluations, and no unresolved incident exists for that service and rule.
haiku-low.q2: Each further breach only updates the incident's breach count and last breach time; no one is paged.
haiku-low.q3: Ten consecutive evaluations below 1% (quiet streak 10 or more) mark it resolved. A later breach opens a new incident.
haiku-low.q4: Primary immediately; secondary 5 minutes later; engineering manager 5 minutes after that, unless acknowledged or resolved.
haiku-low.q5: Push is tried first, SMS only if push errors. Each attempt is logged. Escalation continues regardless, since the next timer is queued before paging.
haiku-low.q6: Everyone successfully reached by push or SMS in page_log gets a resolved notice. Pending escalation timers see resolved and stop.
haiku-low.q7: alert_state row in Postgres per (service, rule). Breach zeroes quiet streak; quiet zeroes breach streak; 1–2% or low-volume resets both.
haiku-low.q8: A unique (service, rule, minute) claim row: only the winner updates streaks and sends. Postgres allows one unresolved incident per service and rule.
haiku-low.q9: Timer fires with a level. If not acked or resolved, the manager sets that level, pages on-call, and queues level 3 only after level 2.
haiku-low.q10: Pager's webhook returns incident and person (echo assumed). Manager marks acked only if still open. Timers read state when firing, so acked incidents stop escalating.
haiku-low.q11: Schedule service is asked at every page, for that service and level, so rotation changes at 09:00 are picked up.
haiku-low.q12: From page_log: the manager reads rows per incident and sends resolved only to people whose push or SMS page succeeded.

sonnet.q1: A breach streak of 3 or more consecutive evaluations (each: trailing 5-min error rate above 2% with at least 500 requests) is sent to the incident manager, and no unresolved incident exists for that (service, rule). Then it inserts a new incident (only one unresolved per service+rule).
sonnet.q2: Evaluators keep sending breach every breaching minute once streak is 3+. Each breach is only recorded on the existing incident (breach count, last breach time); nobody is paged. This includes a new streak of 3 after a reset while the incident is still open.
sonnet.q3: Resolves after 10 consecutive quiet evaluations (below 1%; zero requests counts), when the evaluator sends clear and the manager marks it resolved. A breach after resolution opens a new incident (new id).
sonnet.q4: Level 1 primary is paged immediately on open. A 5-minute timer then pages level 2 secondary (about 5 min after open), and its 5-minute timer pages level 3 engineering manager (about 10 min after open). Each page happens only if the incident is not acked or resolved. After the EM nothing more is sent.
sonnet.q5: The manager calls push, and calls SMS only if push returns an error. Each attempt is written to page_log. A failed page never stops or delays escalation, since the next timer is queued before the page is sent. If the schedule lookup fails or nobody is on call, it writes a page_log row with no person, pages nobody at that level, and the next timer fires as normal.
sonnet.q6: Everyone in page_log who was successfully reached by push or SMS gets a "resolved" notice (via push then SMS). People whose pages all failed and lookup-failure rows are skipped. A failed notice is logged and not retried. Pending timers are not cancelled. When they fire they read the incident, see it is resolved, and stop.
sonnet.q7: In Postgres, in an alert_state row per (service, rule), holding a breach streak and a quiet streak. A breach adds one to the breach streak and zeroes the quiet streak. Below 1% adds one to the quiet streak and zeroes the breach streak. A rate from 1% to 2%, or above 2% with fewer than 500 requests, resets both.
sonnet.q8: Each evaluator tries to insert a row for (service, rule, minute) with a unique key. Only the winner updates streaks in the same transaction and sends breach or clear. The loser does nothing. Postgres also allows only one unresolved incident per (service, rule), so if two inserts race the loser stops and its timer finds no incident and does nothing. No lock or standby is needed.
sonnet.q9: A timer message escalate(incident id, level), queued 5 minutes earlier, triggers the step. The manager reads the incident from Postgres and stops if it is acked or resolved. Otherwise it sets current level, queues the next timer (level 3 after level 2, none after 3), looks up who is on call for that level, and pages them.
sonnet.q10: The Pager calls the incident manager's ack webhook with the incident id and person (echoed back, assumed and listed as an open question). The manager sets acked_by, acked_at and state acked, only if the incident is still open. Pending timers are not cancelled. When they fire they read the incident, see it is acked, and stop. A second ack, or one after resolution, is ignored.
sonnet.q11: At every page, by asking the schedule service who is on call for that service and level right now, for both the initial level 1 page and each escalation. It is not decided in advance.
sonnet.q12: It reads the page_log rows for the incident. Those rows record each attempt's person, channel and result. Everyone with a successful push or SMS gets the notice.
